knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Excluded work needs a written, priced variation approved before work. Doing it, or ignoring the request, is not the correct response.
A missing or unclear exclusion is the usual source of disagreement about what was agreed.
A variation must be written, priced and approved by the named person before the extra work starts. A verbal request is not a variation.
The promises and representations section says not to promise work, results or standards that the contract does not include.

practicalCriteria: Identifies inclusions, exclusions, frequencies and named approvers on a sample contract, and flags at least one vague term.
Refers a simulated verbal variation request to a written, priced approval without starting the work.
Does not promise excluded work, a result, a date or a price in a simulated client conversation.
passRule: Scope, exclusions and approvers identified; verbal variation referred for written approval; no excluded work or promise made. Observed in a desk exercise and a simulated client conversation. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Variation request record with approval field completed
Assessor observation note for the simulated conversation
stopWorkCriteria: Excluded work performed without an approved variation
Result, date or price promised outside the contract
